Free-text notes added by the approver during the review process. May include conditions placed on the approval, scope limitations, or instructions for the provisioning team.
The date and time when the approver rendered an approval or rejection decision on the access request. Null if no decision has been made yet.
Reference to the workforce employee (typically a manager or system owner) who approved or rejected the access request. Null if the request has not yet reached an approval decision.
Reference to the workforce employee record for the individual requesting or on whose behalf access is being requested. Links to the employee master in the workforce domain.
Free-text reason provided when an access request is cancelled before a final approval decision. Captures context such as employee departure, role change, or duplicate request scenarios.
The date and time when the access request was cancelled. Null if the request was not cancelled. Supports lifecycle completeness in audit reporting.

The primary regulatory or compliance framework governing the access being requested (e.g., SOX, PCI DSS, GDPR, HIPAA, OSHA). Used to route requests through appropriate compliance-aware approval workflows and to tag access grants for regulatory reporting.
The cost center code associated with the employee's department at the time of the request. Used for labor cost allocation of IT access management activities and chargebacks.
The date and time when the access request record was first created in the system. May precede submitted_timestamp if the request was saved as a draft.

The highest data classification level of the data or system resources covered by this access request: public, internal, confidential, or restricted. Drives approval workflow complexity and audit requirements.
Self-referencing FK on access_request (delegated_from_access_request_id)
The organizational department of the employee at the time the access request was submitted (e.g., Store Operations, Finance, Supply Chain, Human Resources). Snapshot value for audit trail integrity.
The date from which the requested access should be active. May be a future date for onboarding scenarios or role transitions. Supports scheduled provisioning workflows.

The date on which the requested access should automatically expire or be reviewed for renewal. Null for permanent access grants. Supports time-limited access for contractors, seasonal workers, and emergency access scenarios.

The transaction or business process ID from the Workday HCM system that triggered or is associated with this access request (e.g., a hire, transfer, or termination business process ID). Enables end-to-end traceability between HR events and access provisioning actions.

Indicates whether this request is a break-glass or emergency access request that bypasses standard approval workflows. Emergency access requests require post-hoc review and are subject to enhanced audit scrutiny.

Indicates whether the requested access is classified as privileged (e.g., system administrator, database administrator, payroll administrator). Privileged access requests require additional approval steps and enhanced monitoring.
The job title of the employee at the time the access request was submitted. Captured as a snapshot to support audit reviews even if the employee's role changes after the request is processed.
Free-text business justification provided by the requester explaining why the access is needed. Required for audit and compliance purposes, particularly for elevated or sensitive access requests.

Reference to the retail store or location for which access is being requested, when the request is scoped to a specific store or distribution center. Null for corporate-wide or system-level access requests.
The scheduled date for the next periodic access review or certification of this access grant. Supports access recertification campaigns and compliance with least-privilege policies.

Business urgency assigned to the access request: low (routine, standard SLA), medium (elevated urgency), high (business-impacting delay), critical (emergency or break-glass scenario requiring immediate action). Drives SLA and escalation routing.

The identity (username or system name) that executed the provisioning action in the target system. May be a human IT administrator username or an automated provisioning system identifier. Supports accountability in access audit trails.
The date and time when the approved access was actually provisioned in the target system. Used to measure provisioning SLA compliance (time from approval to provisioning).

Indicates how the access was provisioned once approved: automated (via identity governance platform or SCIM), manual (IT administrator action), or hybrid (partial automation with manual steps). Supports process efficiency analysis.
Free-text explanation provided by the approver when an access request is rejected. Documents the rationale for denial for audit, compliance, and requester feedback purposes.

The HR lifecycle event that triggered this access request, if applicable: new_hire (onboarding provisioning), transfer (location or department change), promotion (role elevation), termination (deprovisioning), leave_of_absence (temporary suspension), rehire (re-provisioning). Null for ad-hoc requests not tied to an HR event.
Human-readable, externally-known reference number assigned to the access request at submission (e.g., AR-2024-000123). Used in communications, audit trails, and helpdesk tickets.

Current workflow state of the access request: draft (saved but not submitted), submitted (awaiting review), pending_approval (under manager/owner review), approved (decision made, awaiting provisioning), rejected (denied), provisioned (access granted in target system), cancelled (withdrawn by requester). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|submitted|pending_approval|approved|rejected|provisioned|cancelled — promote to reference product]

Categorizes the nature of the access request: new_access (first-time provisioning), modify_access (change to existing permissions), remove_access (deprovisioning/offboarding), emergency_access (break-glass or temporary elevated access), role_change (job role transition requiring access realignment).

The specific role, permission set, or access profile being requested within the target system (e.g., Store Manager Read-Only, Payroll Administrator, Inventory Viewer). Aligns with role-based access control (RBAC) definitions.
Reference to the workforce employee who submitted the access request. May differ from employee_id when a manager or HR business partner submits on behalf of another employee.

Indicates whether the requested access requires multi-factor authentication (MFA) enforcement. Typically true for privileged access, remote access, and access to systems containing sensitive retail or financial data.

Indicates whether this access grant requires a scheduled post-provisioning review (e.g., quarterly access certification). Typically true for privileged access, emergency access, and access to sensitive financial or HR systems.

The geographic scope of the access being requested (e.g., a specific store region, country, or global). Relevant for multi-region retail enterprises where access may be scoped to specific geographies for data residency or operational reasons.

Indicates whether the access request exceeded its SLA target fulfillment time. Set to true when the provisioned_timestamp minus submitted_timestamp exceeds sla_target_hours. Used for SLA compliance reporting.
The target number of business hours within which the access request should be fulfilled from submission, as defined by the applicable SLA policy. Varies by priority level and access category.

The channel through which the access request was initiated: self_service_portal (employee self-service), manager_initiated (submitted by a manager on behalf of a direct report), hr_system (triggered by an HR event such as hire or transfer in the HCM platform), automated_onboarding (system-generated for new hires), helpdesk (submitted via IT helpdesk).
The date and time when the access request was formally submitted by the requester. This is the principal business event timestamp marking the start of the request lifecycle.

Specific module or sub-component within the target system for which access is requested (e.g., Payroll within Workday, Inventory Management within WMS, Financial Reporting within ERP). Provides granularity beyond system_name.

Name of the application, system, or platform for which access is being requested (e.g., Workday HCM, POS System, Warehouse Management System, Databricks, SAP). Free-text to accommodate the full breadth of retail enterprise systems.

Reference number of the corresponding IT service management ticket (e.g., ServiceNow, Jira) created to fulfill the access request. Enables cross-system traceability between the access request record and the provisioning work order.

became.before: This association product represents the Receipt Event between inbound_shipment and purchase_order. It captures the operational mapping between ASNs (Advance Ship Notices) and purchase orders during receiving operations at distribution centers. Each record links one inbound shipment to one purchase order with receipt-specific attributes including received quantities, timestamps, variances, and quality holds. This is the SSOT for PO-level receipt tracking, supplier performance measurement, and three-way match reconciliation (PO-Receipt-Invoice).. Existence Justification: In retail distribution operations, a single inbound shipment (ASN) routinely contains goods for multiple purchase orders consolidated by the supplier or carrier for efficiency. Conversely, a single purchase order is frequently split across multiple shipments due to partial fulfillments, supplier capacity constraints, or phased delivery schedules. The receipt mapping between ASNs and POs is actively managed during receiving operations with specific data tracked per PO-shipment combination including received quantities, timestamps, variances, and quality holds.
became.after: Records the physical receipt of purchase order shipments at distribution centers, capturing quantities received, quality inspections, temperature readings, dock assignments, and variance tracking against expected deliveries.

became.before: EDI transaction log for supply chain document exchanges with suppliers, 3PLs, and trading partners via SPS Commerce, TrueCommerce, or similar VAN. Captures transaction set type (850 PO, 855 PO Ack, 856 ASN, 810 Invoice, 860 PO Change, 997 Functional Ack), trading partner GLN/DUNS, transmission timestamp, direction (inbound/outbound), document reference, processing status, error codes, retry count, and compliance score. Enables EDI compliance monitoring against retailer routing guide requirements, SLA breach detection for late ASN/invoice, integration health dashboards, and trading partner onboarding validation.
became.after: [References SSOT: supplier.supplier_edi_transaction] Supply chain operational view of EDI transactions for DC and logistics operations. References supplier.supplier_edi_transaction as the authoritative EDI record. Adds supply chain context like routing guide versions and SLA tracking.

affected_objects.before: This association product represents the Receipt Event between inbound_shipment and purchase_order. It captures the operational mapping between ASNs (Advance Ship Notices) and purchase orders during receiving operations at distribution centers. Each record links one inbound shipment to one purchase order with receipt-specific attributes including received quantities, timestamps, variances, and quality holds. This is the SSOT for PO-level receipt tracking, supplier performance measurement, and three-way match reconciliation (PO-Receipt-Invoice).. Existence Justification: In retail distribution operations, a single inbound shipment (ASN) routinely contains goods for multiple purchase orders consolidated by the supplier or carrier for efficiency. Conversely, a single purchase order is frequently split across multiple shipments due to partial fulfillments, supplier capacity constraints, or phased delivery schedules. The receipt mapping between ASNs and POs is actively managed during receiving operations with specific data tracked per PO-shipment combination including received quantities, timestamps, variances, and quality holds.
affected_objects.after: Records the physical receipt of purchase order shipments at distribution centers, capturing quantities received, quality inspections, temperature readings, dock assignments, and variance tracking against expected deliveries.

affected_objects.before: EDI transaction log for supply chain document exchanges with suppliers, 3PLs, and trading partners via SPS Commerce, TrueCommerce, or similar VAN. Captures transaction set type (850 PO, 855 PO Ack, 856 ASN, 810 Invoice, 860 PO Change, 997 Functional Ack), trading partner GLN/DUNS, transmission timestamp, direction (inbound/outbound), document reference, processing status, error codes, retry count, and compliance score. Enables EDI compliance monitoring against retailer routing guide requirements, SLA breach detection for late ASN/invoice, integration health dashboards, and trading partner onboarding validation.
affected_objects.after: [References SSOT: supplier.supplier_edi_transaction] Supply chain operational view of EDI transactions for DC and logistics operations. References supplier.supplier_edi_transaction as the authoritative EDI record. Adds supply chain context like routing guide versions and SLA tracking.

lineage.vibe: Fix the 13 data-type errors in the customer schema where columns were generated by description without checking the type (e.g. monetary, count, or rate columns stored as the wrong type). These break SUM/AVG/comparison operations and force casts in every downstream query; they are correctness bugs, not taste issues, and MUST be corrected.
lineage.interpretation: Fix 13 data-type correctness bugs in customer schema

lineage.vibe: Fix the schema/database name mismatch: the MVM customer schema file is named _v1_mvm.sql but the DDL writes into the retail_ecm catalog, so deploying both MVM and ECM blows away the first. The MVM and ECM schemas must target DISTINCT catalogs (retail_mvm vs retail_ecm), not both writing to retail_ecm.
lineage.interpretation: Separate MVM and ECM into distinct catalogs to prevent overwrites

lineage.vibe: The customer database comment promises 'Single source of truth for all customer identity, profiles, households, segments…' but there is no household table; ensure the household table actually exists in the customer domain so the comment is truthful.
lineage.interpretation: Ensure household table exists to match database comment

lineage.vibe: Perform a vendor-strip pass on column comments: replace specific vendor names with neutral descriptors. Specifically: Informatica MDM → 'the customer master data system', Salesforce Commerce Cloud → 'the e-commerce platform', Salesforce Service Cloud → 'the case management system', SAP CAR → 'the retail analytics platform', and drop 'Nike' examples entirely. Implementation detail of which vendor tool is used does not belong in a reference data model.
lineage.interpretation: Strip ~15 vendor names from comments, replace with neutral descriptors

lineage.vibe: Restrict enum constraints to abstract type categories only, not specific vendor brands or providers. For example payment_method should constrain payment_method_type ∈ {credit_card, debit_card, wallet, gift_card, store_credit, bnpl}, but card_brand and wallet_provider should be free STRING with a comment listing 'common values include…'. Do not enum-constrain card brands (visa, mastercard, amex, etc.), BNPL providers (Klarna, Affirm, etc.), or wallet providers.
lineage.interpretation: Limit enums to abstract type categories; brands/providers as free STRING

lineage.vibe: De-duplicate marketing consent: the same logical fact ('customer agreed to receive emails') is currently modeled in four places (profile opt-in flags, account marketing consent fields, contact opt-in fields, and the dedicated consent table). Pick the consent table as the single source of truth and delete the 11 redundant opt-in flags scattered across profile, account, and contact (e.g. profile.email_opt_in_flag, profile.sms_opt_in_flag, profile.marketing_consent_flag, profile.gdpr_consent_flag, profile.ccpa_opt_out_flag, account.marketing_opt_in, account.data_sharing_consent, account.marketing_opt_in_date, account.marketing_opt_out_date, contact.opt_in_marketing, contact.opt_in_transactional, contact.opt_in_date, contact.opt_out_date).
lineage.interpretation: Consolidate consent into the consent table; remove redundant opt-in flags

lineage.vibe: The preference table is an EAV-ish god-table: preference_category mixes 12 unrelated concepts (communication_channel, product_category_affinity, dietary_restriction, brand_preference, store_preference, language, notification_frequency, privacy_consent, marketing_opt_in, delivery_preference, payment_method_preference, shopping_time_preference). Split it into focused tables — separate communication_preference, dietary_restriction, and a small customer_attribute(key, value) extensibility table for the long tail.
lineage.interpretation: Split preference god-table into focused tables plus a key/value extensibility table

lineage.vibe: service_case (52 columns, 18+ FKs reaching into compliance, ecommerce, fulfillment, supplychain, supplier, store, merchandising, pricing, promotion, loyalty) is customer-service operational data, not customer master data; move it out of the customer domain into its own service domain.
lineage.interpretation: Re-home service_case to a dedicated service domain

lineage.vibe: segment and customer_membership are marketing-analytics constructs, not customer identity/master data; move them out of the customer domain into a marketing or customer_intelligence domain.
lineage.interpretation: Re-home segment and customer_membership to marketing/customer_intelligence domain

lineage.vibe: The consent table (with full GDPR/CCPA scaffolding) is regulator-facing, not identity; move it from the customer domain into a privacy or compliance domain, keeping the table almost as-is. A truly minimum-viable customer schema is profile + address + contact + consent (+ optional account for B2B), about 4-5 tables, not 10.
lineage.interpretation: Move consent to privacy/compliance domain; minimal customer = profile/address/contact/consent(+optional account)

lineage.vibe: Remove computed-from-transactions derived metrics stored on master tables: profile.last_interaction_date, profile.last_purchase_date, profile.cltv_score, profile.cac_amount, profile.nps_score, account.total_lifetime_orders, account.last_transaction_date, account.outstanding_balance. These should be metric views or materialized views, not columns on master records, because storing them invites write amplification and staleness (OLAP bleeding into OLTP).
lineage.interpretation: Remove derived metric columns from profile/account; relocate to metric views

lineage.vibe: Resolve profile vs account overlap: profile and account share large overlap (both have preferred_channel, marketing opt-in flags, status). Keep profile as the identity entity and make account optional, existing only for B2B/wholesale relationships, so most B2C rows have null or default account rows.
lineage.interpretation: Make profile the identity entity; account optional for B2B only

lineage.vibe: Move payment_method out of the customer master schema: storing cardholder_name puts the table in PCI DSS scope, transitively dragging everything joined to it into audit territory. Keep tokenized payment instruments in a vault-adjacent schema (e.g. finance.payment_instrument) so non-payment workloads stay out of PCI scope.
lineage.interpretation: Re-home payment_method to a vault-adjacent finance schema to limit PCI scope

lineage.vibe: Clean up tags and metadata: remove the auto-generated dbx_business_glossary_term tags that are mostly just the column name capitalized (e.g. account_id → 'Account ID'), which is noise not glossary. Keep the useful PII tags (dbx_pii_name, dbx_pii_phone, dbx_pii_email, dbx_pii_dob, dbx_pii_address, dbx_pii_financial). Pick a single source between dbx_value_regex tags and the column-comment text rather than duplicating; cutting glossary noise shortens the file ~40%.
lineage.interpretation: Strip noise glossary tags, keep PII tags, de-duplicate regex vs comment

lineage.vibe: Reduce and correct the 49 cross-domain FKs originating from the customer schema; customer is the root and should depend on almost nothing. Transactions depend on customer, not the other way around. Keep sensible references like profile.location_id into store (preferred store) but remove reversed-direction FKs like consent.promo_campaign_id into promotion (campaigns reference consent records, not the other way). Fix the many FKs whose dependency-arrow direction is reversed.
lineage.interpretation: Prune/reverse incorrect cross-domain FKs from customer; customer is the root

lineage.vibe: Apply consistent SCD pattern: master tables profile, account, and address currently use only last_modified_timestamp (destructive update, no history) while other tables (preference, contact, segment, customer_membership) have SCD Type 2 effective_start_date/effective_end_date/status. For a 'golden record' with GDPR audit trails, the master tables (profile, account) need SCD-2 or change-data-capture, not destructive update.
lineage.interpretation: Add SCD-2/CDC history to profile, account, address master tables

lineage.vibe: Resolve customer_type confusion: profile.customer_type ∈ {individual, corporate, employee, vip, wholesale} conflates entity type (individual vs corporate), classification (vip — also exists as vip_flag and account_tier=vip), and relationship (employee — also exists as employee_flag). Separate what kind of legal entity (individual/organization) from what role they play to us (consumer/employee/wholesale_buyer/...) and remove the redundant vip/employee duplications.
lineage.interpretation: Separate legal-entity type from role; eliminate vip/employee redundancy

lineage.vibe: Keep the genuinely good aspects: sensible top-level domain decomposition, the MVM/ECM product split, consistent dbx_pii_* PII tagging for masking/access control, the thorough GDPR/CCPA consent table (keep almost as-is, just re-homed), reasonable category-list enum constraints (status values, lifecycle stages), domain-aware column comments (strip vendor names only), and accurate cross-domain FK justification comments that explain why a relationship exists.
lineage.interpretation: Preserve good aspects: domain decomposition, MVM/ECM split, PII tags, consent scaffolding, category enums, FK justifications

lineage.vibe: Aim for a vendor-neutral reference model that captures the intersection of universal retail concepts with extensibility hooks for everything else, rather than the union of every retailer's opinions. The MVM in particular must be minimal; be opinionated only where the industry has genuine consensus.

  dimensions:
    - name: "alert_type"
      expr: alert_type

      expr: alert_status
      comment: "Current status of alert (new, acknowledged, in-progress, resolved, closed, false-positive)"
    - name: "severity_level"
      expr: severity_level
      comment: "Severity classification (critical, high, medium, low)"
    - name: "escalation_level"
      expr: escalation_level
      comment: "Current escalation tier (L1, L2, L3, executive)"
    - name: "false_positive_flag"
      expr: false_positive_flag
      comment: "Whether alert was determined to be a false positive"
    - name: "notification_sent_flag"
      expr: notification_sent_flag
      comment: "Whether notification was successfully sent"
    - name: "notification_channel"
      expr: notification_channel
      comment: "Channel used for alert notification (email, SMS, Slack, PagerDuty)"
    - name: "business_entity_type"
      expr: business_entity_type
      comment: "Type of business entity that triggered the alert"
    - name: "data_source"
      expr: data_source
      comment: "Source system or process that generated the alert"
    - name: "triggered_date"
      expr: DATE(triggered_timestamp)
      comment: "Date the alert was triggered for time-series analysis"
  measures:
    - name: "total_alerts"
      expr: COUNT(1)
      comment: "Total number of alerts generated"
    - name: "total_resolved_alerts"
      expr: SUM(CASE WHEN alert_status IN ('resolved', 'closed') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
      comment: "Number of alerts that have been resolved or closed"
    - name: "total_false_positives"
      expr: SUM(CASE WHEN false_positive_flag = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
      comment: "Number of alerts identified as false positives"
    - name: "alert_resolution_rate"
      expr: ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN alert_status IN ('resolved', 'closed') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(1), 0), 2)
      comment: "Percentage of alerts that have been resolved"
    - name: "false_positive_rate"
      expr: ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN false_positive_flag = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(1), 0), 2)
      comment: "Percentage of alerts that were false positives - key quality metric"
    - name: "notification_success_rate"
      expr: ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN notification_sent_flag = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(1), 0), 2)
      comment: "Percentage of alerts where notification was successfully sent"
    - name: "avg_actual_value"
      expr: AVG(CAST(actual_value AS DOUBLE))
      comment: "Average actual value that triggered alerts"
    - name: "avg_threshold_value"
      expr: AVG(CAST(threshold_value AS DOUBLE))
      comment: "Average threshold value for alert triggers"
    - name: "avg_variance_amount"
      expr: AVG(CAST(variance_amount AS DOUBLE))
      comment: "Average variance between actual and threshold values"
    - name: "distinct_kpi_definitions"
      expr: COUNT(DISTINCT kpi_definition_id)
      comment: "Number of unique KPI definitions that generated alerts"
    - name: "distinct_business_entities"
      expr: COUNT(DISTINCT business_entity_id)
      comment: "Number of unique business entities that triggered alerts"
$$
